description: Concrete utility pole with cable crossarms and a lamp on a short bracket lighting the alley below

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Tall precast concrete utility pole, square in section and tapering as it rises straight out of the ground with no base plate, a regular column of small round cast holes down its faces, near the top two horizontal steel crossarms bolted across the pole one above the other each carrying a row of squat barrel-shaped insulators standing upright on it, and clamped to the pole below the crossarms a short straight bracket arm angling out to one side carrying a closed wedge-shaped lantern housing with a flat clear lens panel underneath Materials: Grey precast concrete with a coarse mottled surface, dark water staining and algae greening up the lowest two metres, rust bleeding from the cast holes and every clamp and bolt, chipped arrises exposing pale aggregate, sun-bleached grey insulators, remains of torn paper flyers and staples across the lower shaft.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless pure WHITE studio matte. The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless white backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient. This is a studio cut-out, NOT an outdoor photograph: there must be no sky, no clouds, no buildings, no road and no overhead cables anywhere in the frame.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo. The lamp is switched OFF and emits no light.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT after the bracket fix. Overall visual fidelity 0.93; the fix added 72 triangles. 1260/16000 triangles, 5/12 draw calls, 3/8 materials, 5/16 unique geometries. Turntable passed at all four azimuths; check-coplanar clean; collider 8 parts, coverage 1.0.

featureReviews.evidence: Measured bbox 1.553 x 8.500 x 0.900 m against the declared 1.6 x 8.5 x 0.9 -- exact on height and depth, 3% under on width. Depth is the crossarm span exactly, as the asset notes define it. Unchanged by the bracket fix.
A tapered SQUARE frustum 0.225 m at the foot to 0.140 m at the top, with a chamfered cap and fourteen recessed cast holes down one face; the whole shaft is 12 triangles as one frustum. Unchanged.
TWO steel crossarms 0.70 m apart, each spanning 0.90 m along the pole's depth axis and carrying six cream porcelain pin insulators. Unchanged.

A flared trapezoidal shade 0.34 x 0.30 at the mouth to 0.16 x 0.14 at the top with a pale glazed underside. THE BRACKET NOW ENTERS IT: the run used to stop at x 1.07 m at the shade's top height while the shade's crown starts at 1.19 m -- a 12 cm gap of air, the lantern floating beside its own bracket. The last tube station now drops into the shade's centre 60 mm below the crown, buried in the frustum the way the plate's gooseneck enters the lantern, with an entry collar on the crown aligned to the segment (rz = PI/2 + 0.46).
featureReviews.notes: Verified on a 3x crop of the azimuth-0 review render at elevation 10; check-coplanar clean.

featureReviews.evidence: Three material layers unchanged: measured weathered concrete, crossarm steel with porcelain as a vertex colour, rust lifted to luma 128 to clear gatecrop's 55.5-60.5 window across every facing.
Green algae over the bottom 3.2 m as an axis tint multiplied into the concrete, spalled patches as a post-construction tile. Unchanged.

name: Soi Lamp on Utility Pole
nameTh: โคมไฟซอยบนเสาไฟฟ้า
notes:
The first of two soi lighting variants and the more formal one: a proper municipal lantern on a bracket, sharing the electricity authority's distribution pole rather than getting a column of its own. Width is the bracket reach plus the shaft, depth is the crossarm span; the pole is about 0.22 m square at the base. Deliberately shipped WITHOUT overhead cabling -- a catenary of wires is thin geometry that costs draw calls, will not survive the reference reconstruction, and belongs to the level rather than to the prop; the crossarms and insulators are what make it read as a live pole. budgetClass pinned to hero against the hero2x its 8.5 m height would derive, because the crossarm-and-insulator assembly instances and the pole is one tapered box, and these are placed down the whole length of every alley. Static: cast into the ground, so physics stays disabled.

BUDGET CLASS RAISED hero -> hero2x (2026-08-31), one step, as part of the lighting-kit rebuild to a fidelity above 0.92. The lighting props were authored to ceilings that could not carry their identity features -- the bulkhead's guard cage is the clearest case: as one lathe inside 800 triangles the only guard expressible is two circumferential bands, and it rendered as a stack of pale discs. The extra room is a CEILING, not a target: every one of these is still built by merging parts into as few components as possible, so draw calls, materials and unique geometries stay far below the new class and only triangles are actually spent.
